back_translation: Behold, on the mountains, the feet of one who brings good news, who proclaims peace! O Judah, celebrate your feasts and fulfill your vows, for the wicked will never again pass through you; he is utterly cut off.
O Nineveh, the destroyer has come up against you. Guard the fortress, watch the road, brace your loins, gather all your strength to the utmost.
For the LORD will restore the splendor of Jacob like the splendor of Israel, for plunderers have plundered them and ruined the branches of their vine.
The shields of his warriors are red, and the soldiers are clothed in scarlet; the chariots flash like fire on the day they are made ready, and the cypress spears are brandished.
The chariots race through the streets, rushing back and forth in the squares; they look like torches and dart about like flashes of lightning.
The king summons his officers; they stumble as they advance; they hasten to the city wall, and the protective shield is set up.
The river gates are thrown open, and the palace melts away.
It is decreed: she is stripped bare and carried off; her slave girls moan like the sound of doves, beating their breasts.
Nineveh is like a pool whose waters are draining away. 'Stop! Stop!' they cry, but no one turns back.
Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold! For there is no end to the hoarded treasure—an abundance of every precious thing.
She is empty, plundered, and laid waste; hearts melt and knees give way; every waist is in anguish, and every face grows pale.
Where is the den of the lions, the cave where the young lions fed—where the lion, the lioness, and the lion's cubs prowled, with nothing to make them afraid?
The lion tore enough prey for his cubs and strangled prey for his lionesses; he filled his caves with prey and his dens with what he had torn.

The LORD of Hosts declares: Behold, I am against you. I will burn your chariots into smoke, and the sword will devour your young lions. I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers will no longer be heard.
